sentences.text:
By way of the present writ petition, the petitioners seek quashing of FIR bearing no. 632/2022,
registered at Police Station Najafgarh, District- Dwarka, New Delhi, for the commission of offence punishable under Sections 498A/406/34 of Indian Penal Code, 1860 (hereafter IPC ) on the basis of the settlement/MOU.
2.
This Court notes that the learned counsel for respondent no.2 had appeared through video conferencing on 22.04.2025 and an undertaking was given that the complainant will appear on 18.07.2025.
It was clarified that in case she does not appear on 18.07.2025, bailable warrants will be issued against her.
On 18.07.2025, the Court was not in session, though the appearance of learned counsel for respondent no. 2 was marked, however, the presence of respondent no. 2 has not been marked.
Further, again on 03.09.2025, respondent no. 2 did not appear before this Court.
This is a digitally signed order.
The authenticity of the order can be re-verified from Delhi High Court Order Portal by scanning the QR code shown above.
The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 03/12/2025 at 21:31:22 3.
This Court has taken note of the fact that despite a direction issued on 22.04.2025, respondent no. 2 has not appeared before this Court, including today.

sentences.text: The learned counsel for respondent no. 2 appearing through video conferencing repeatedly stated that respondent no. 2 will appear before this Court.
She also disputes that the MOU has been placed on record.
She further states that the petitioners are not complying with the same.
5. The learned counsel appearing for the petitioner states that they have partially abided by the said MOU.
6. Be that as it may, since the petition has been filed with an MOU of respondent no. 2, it was the duty of respondent no. 2 to have appeared before this Court today.
The matter has been coming up before this Court for last four dates.
7. Today again, the learned counsel appearing for respondent no. 2 through video conferencing states that respondent no. 2 has some medical problem.

8. Be that as it may, the learned counsel for respondent no. 2 is directed to ensure that respondent no. 2 appears before this Court on the next date of hearing and in case, she does not appear, bailable warrants will be issued against her.

9. At request, list on 08.12.2025.
10.
The order be uploaded on the website forthwith.
DR. SWARANA KANTA SHARMA, J DECEMBER 01, 2025/
A / GJ
